threads.body: `gateHolding` writes a regular temp file, so no test opens a real FIFO. The blocking open, blocking read and end-of-input path that `otel-conformance-obi` depends on aren't tested, and that's why the JDK 21 `Illegal seek` above passes every test here. Could one test create the gate with `mkfifo` (skipped when not on Linux) and write the release byte from a second thread?

replies.body: Added two mkfifo tests (Linux only), with the launcher side writing from a second thread. With the old readAllBytes() they fail on Java 21 with waiting at the gate: Illegal seek; with the loop they pass on 21 and 25.

threads.body: Nit: this checks that the constant equals its own text. A test that would actually catch drift would compare it to the Python launcher's `GATE_VARIABLE`, or you could drop this test. Also on line 26, the `(String) null` cast isn't needed: there's only one single-argument overload.

Question about the design: the gate call is repeated in 14 launcher `main`s. Go does it once (`scenario.Run`/`RunServer` call `WaitAtGate`), and `waitAtGate()` already does nothing when `OTEL_CONFORMANCE_GATE` is unset. Did you consider calling it once from the shared launcher path? Then the `obi` projects wouldn't each need a hand-written `main`, and the upcoming client and database OBI packages would get it for free. I can see why you kept `ScenarioLauncher` untouched, so I'm fine either way.

replies.body: Thats a good point, I changed it so the ScenarioLauncher waits at the gate before it calls the scenario's main (a no-op when OTEL_CONFORMANCE_GATE is unset), each shared server scenario has a main, and the obi projects have no sources of their own; their run: lines name the shared class.
